solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fill to excess: meal price reduced by a penny (11)

indicatorNotes.reduced by: the meal is made smaller by taking the penny out

blocks.note: P for penny, taken out of SUPPER to leave SUPER

annotation.surface: A diner grumbles about a meal whose price has been knocked down by a single penny.
annotation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for a penny; take one P out of SUPPER and the meal becomes SUPER.
annotation.definitionFit: To supercharge something is to fill or load it beyond the normal amount.

entries.clue: Broth — you left out bread to go with it? (3)

indicatorNotes.left out: YOU, as the letter U, is omitted

blocks.note: U sounds like 'you' in text-speak; this letter is the one left out of the broth

annotation.surface: Someone serving broth notices the bread has been forgotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broth' looks like the definition but is wordplay; the definition leans on it, since a sop is bread dipped in soup, and 'it' is the broth.
annotation.definitionFit: A sop is a piece of bread soaked in broth or gravy.

entries.clue: Rogue protein bears at last removed from porridge (5)

indicatorNotes.removed from: the last letter of 'bears' is taken out of the prison word

blocks.note: porridge is British slang for a jail sentence, hence prison

annotation.surface: Bears again: something nasty is finally kept out of the porridge, as in Goldilocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is not breakfast here: in British slang doing porridge means serving time, so it gives PRISON, which loses its S.
annotation.definitionFit: A prion is a misfolded protein that causes disease, such as mad cow disease.

entries.clue: Run round balloon where aliens arrived? (7)

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

annotation.surface: Someone runs around a weather balloon at the site of a supposed UFO landing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the story itself: the 1947 Roswell debris was officially a weather balloon.
annotation.definitionFit: Roswell, New Mexico, is where a UFO supposedly crashed in 1947; the question mark admits it is legend.

entries.clue: Stop woman receiving fine for misleading statement (4-5)

indicatorNotes.receiving: a person receiving a guest takes them in, so HALT holds the F inside itself

blocks.note: F for fine, as on pencil grades

annotation.surface: A woman is stopped and fined for making a misleading statement.
annotation.walkthrough: F sits inside HALT, and RUTH follows; 'woman' in a clue often stands for any girl's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A half-truth is a statement that is partly true but meant to mislead.

entries.clue: Correspondence: Henry in line with the writer (5)

indicatorNotes.in: Henry is placed in the line the way a passenger sits in a train, so H goes inside RY

blocks.note: H is the physics symbol for the henry
the writer is the setter, ME

annotation.surface: A letter writer lines up with a man called Henry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' suggests letters, but here it is a matching of sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyme is the correspondence of sound between word endings.

entries.clue: Little animal one’s dearest possession (3-4)

blocks.note: from Nathan's parable in the Bible

annotation.surface: A pet lamb is someone's most treasured possession.
annotation.walkthrough: In 2 Samuel, Nathan tells of a poor man whose one ewe lamb, his only treasure, is taken by a rich man; the phrase came to mean a dearest possession.
annotation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young female sheep, and figuratively the one thing a person holds most dear.

entries.clue: Duck on cape with black swan (3)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, 'on' puts the duck after the cape

blocks.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
B for black, as on pencils

annotation.surface: A duck sits on a headland beside a black swan.
annotation.walkthrough: The birds are a decoy: 'Duck' is the cricket zero and 'black swan' splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: A cob is the specific word for a male swan, as a pen is a female; a species-level definition by example.

entries.clue: Hot treacle almost spoiled pudding (9)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: the letters are ruined, then rebuilt

annotation.surface: Hot treacle, not quite ruined, turns into a dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is fodder too, not H, which is why the letter count works.
annotation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a baked pudding of fruit in a case of bread or sponge.

entries.clue: British ladies perhaps prepare spread: it’s juicy (5,6)

blocks.note: the ladies is a toilet, a loo in British usage
to do a meal is to prepare it

annotation.surface: British women make a spread of food and gossip about something juicy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' is the ladies' room; LOO is the British word for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A blood orange is a red-fleshed, notably juicy orange.

entries.clue: Earl introduced to clerical writer (9)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: E is put inside the word for clerical

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earl

annotation.surface: A nobleman is presented to a writer who works as a clerk.
annotation.walkthrough: E goes between the T and the L of PRIESTLY, so the clerical word needs no respelling to hold the earl.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: J. B. Priestley wrote novels such as The Good Companions and plays including An Inspector Calls.

entries.clue: Books exist, reflecting writer’s inspiration (5)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: a reflection shows things back to front

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

annotation.surface: Books really exist that mirror what inspires a writer.
annotation.walkthrough: OT and NT (the two Testaments) are the usual 'books' in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of a poet's inspiration.

entries.clue: Most crackers auntie regularly dipped in relish (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at every second step
indicatorNotes.dipped in: the letters go inside the relish word

annotation.surface: An aunt dunks crackers into a relish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' is British slang for crazy, so 'most crackers' is a superlative adjective, not biscuits.
annotation.definitionFit: Crackers is informal British for mad or wildly eccentric, so its superlative matches the zany person who clowns about beyond everyone else.

entries.clue: Old suit, worn regularly, clothes idiot in life drifting around (11)

indicatorNotes.clothes: ZOOT and ON dress the idiot, wrapping round it

blocks.note: a plank is British slang for a dimwit

annotation.surface: An idiot drifts through life dressed in an old suit that is worn only occasionally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Life drifting around' reads like a description of the idiot, but it defines the tiny animals that float with sea currents.
annotation.definitionFit: Zooplankton are tiny animals that drift in the sea.

entries.clue: Returning Irishman in Scots river sent message (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the Irishman goes inside the river

annotation.surface: An Irishman heads home by boat along a Scottish river and sends word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returning' covers the river too, not just the Irishman: build the whole thing, then reverse it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: posting a note through an electronic inbox is how most messages get sent today.

entries.clue: Waste from Cornish runner (5)

blocks.note: from, as in 'a man of Kent'
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, a runner

annotation.surface: Rubbish thrown out by an athlete from Cornwall.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river; the Fal reaches the sea at Falmouth, in the English county of Cornwall.
annotation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails of a butchered animal, historically treated as waste.

entries.clue: Shape revealed in crack (6,3)

blocks.note: a secret that is out has been revealed

annotation.surface: An outline shows through a crack in a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack' is a verb here, as in cracking a code.
annotation.definitionFit: Cracking a code or puzzle means solving it by working through the reasoning, an everyday idiom.

entries.clue: Labour wants clearing banks for distributing capital (4,5)

indicatorNotes.clearing banks: the outer letters, the banks, of 'wants' are cleared away
indicatorNotes.distributing: the letters are spread around anew

blocks.note: wANTs without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: The Labour party wants the clearing banks to share out money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clearing banks' reads as UK finance, but it tells you to strip the edges from 'wants'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this city is the seat of government of Mongolia, whose largest settlement it also is.

entries.clue: Food in a resort sweetheart served up (9)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, 'up' reverses the letters

annotation.surface: A couple at a spa resort have food served by a sweetheart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Served up' sounds like dishing out food, which suits the surface, but in a down clue it means written upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A broad definition by example: the tender spears of this plant are a prized spring vegetable.

entries.clue: Kindle’s really cool guide for pilots (9)

annotation.surface: A reader praises the Kindle e-reader as a great guide for airline pilots.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital K makes Kindle look like the e-reader, but it is the verb; 'pilots' are ship pilots, not airline ones.
annotation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel with a beacon that guides ships' pilots.

entries.clue: Vandalised public transport depot loses millions (7)

indicatorNotes.loses: a depot that loses something no longer has it, so the M is dropped from the word

annotation.surface: A tram depot is wrecked and costs a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: TRAMSHED minus M is TRASHED.
annotation.definitionFit: Something trashed has been wrecked, as by vandals.

entries.clue: Lustre of small chicken incubating a little egg? (5)

indicatorNotes.incubating: the hen sits on the egg's letter, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.a little: only a little of 'egg', its first letter

annotation.surface: The gloss of a small hen sitting on a tiny egg.
annotation.walkthrough: E goes into HEN, making HEEN, after S; the question mark admits a first letter is a very little egg.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name the soft glow that polished silk or hair gives off when light strikes it.

entries.clue: Firm ruined can shut (7)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A company went bust and could close.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' tempts as a company in the surface, but it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for steadfast: a supporter who never wavers is described both ways.

entries.clue: North country area includes very serene place (7)

indicatorNotes.includes: a group that includes someone has them within it, so the V sits inside IRAN

annotation.surface: A northern rural area contains a spot of great tranquillity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North country' reads as northern England, but it splits: N, then IRAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state or place of perfect peace.

entries.clue: I’m going to pass on gold rings (5)

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass on is to die

annotation.surface: Someone plans to hand down their gold rings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rings' is a verb, surrounding; the gold rings of the surface are a decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: Adieu, farewell, is what you say when you are going.

entries.clue: Something genuine seen in the round? (4,3)

annotation.definition: Something genuine seen in the round?

blocks.note: reads as any authentic article, but it is the drink whose name starts with REAL, the genuine sort
suggests theatre in the round; the setter means a round of drinks bought at the pub

annotation.surface: A riddle about something authentic viewed from every side, like theatre in the round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the round' suggests theatre or sculpture, but it is a round of drinks; the genuine thing is REAL ale, traditional cask beer.
annotation.definitionFit: Real ale is traditionally brewed cask beer, often bought in a round of drinks.

entries.clue: Pervasive quality of memory cherished by reformed drinkers (5)

indicatorNotes.cherished by: something cherished is held close in an embrace, so ROM is held inside AA

annotation.surface: Recovering alcoholics fondly remember the smell of drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pervasive quality of' looks like part of the wordplay, but it defines an aroma, which pervades.
annotation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive quality that pervades something, as a smell does.

entries.clue: Canine say excessively bony: no home (5)

indicatorNotes.no home: IN, meaning at home, is removed

annotation.surface: A stray dog is far too skinny and has nowhere to live.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but the definition is a canine tooth, and 'say' marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'say': the pointed eye teeth beside the incisors are called canines.

entries.clue: Resourceful island using one at sea (9)

indicatorNotes.at sea: confused, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An islander resourcefully makes use of a single boat at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: I starts the answer; the other eight letters come from mixing up USING ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a person clever at inventing solutions from whatever is at hand.

entries.clue: Down current ignored in Egyptian port (3)

indicatorNotes.ignored in: the current's letter is left out of the port

blocks.note: Port Said, at the north end of the Suez Canal
I is the physics symbol for electric current, removed

annotation.surface: An ocean current is overlooked in an Egyptian harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads like a direction, but it is the adjective for low in spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: An everyday idiom: feeling low in spirits or glum is described as being down.

entries.clue: Head in large cask rolled back (3)

indicatorNotes.rolled back: the cask is turned round, reversing its letters

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel

annotation.surface: Someone's head is stuck in a barrel that is rolled backwards.
annotation.walkthrough: Casks are rolled, so 'rolled back' suits the surface and the reversal equally.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal slang, as in 'use your nut' or headbutting someone, known as nutting them.

entries.clue: Duke left unscathed after crashing in Germany (11)

indicatorNotes.crashing: the letters are smashed and reassembled

annotation.surface: A duke walks away uninjured from a car crash in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: D stays put at the front; L and UNSCATHED are jumbled to make EUTSCHLAND.
annotation.definitionFit: The native-language name: speakers there call their own country this, rather than the English form.
